newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Ericsson tops ADRs.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Ericsson tops ADRs.

text.p: Swedish telecommunications company Ericsson was New York's most heavily traded American Depositary Receipt (ADR) on Wednesday in a mostly slow day.
Traders called the ADR market generally quiet as investors waited for Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan to complete his testimony on economy policy before a Senate panel.
Swedish telecommunications equipment maker LM Ericsson rose 9/16 to 32-13/16 in moderate volume of 1.3 million shares in early afternoon.
Ericsson was the most heavily traded ADR on the New York exchanges.
Construction company Grupo Mexicano de Desarollo was unchanged at midday at 2-3/8 on volume of 1.1 million shares, many times the normal daily activity.
Trade included a single block of 1.08 million shares. Further details were not immediately available.

Level One ADRs in Brazil's state-owned mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce were at a bid of 25-5/8 and ask of 26, or unchanged from Tuesday, after the government set a price for the company's privatization, traders said.

The reformist government set a minimum price of 10.4 billion reais, or 26.67 reais a share, for the company in the biggest privatization in Latin American history. The initial block sale of 45 percent of the government's share will take place April 29.

Level One ADRs trade on the National Association of Securities Dealers' over-the-counter Bulletin Board. The Sao Paulo exchange halted trade in Companhia Vale do Rio Doce before the sale announcement.

Among other ADRs, French industrial group Alcatel Alsthom Cie Generale d'Electricite' rose one to 22. Advancers narrowly led decliners by 256 to 241 among 807 ADRs. Volume in early afternoon was 39.4 million shares.
